text:
tom: FYI incoming SWE Arjun's J-1 ends 2026-08-01 and counsel says a waiver might be required before he can start onsite. can people-ops summarize what this means for start date, relocation, and benefits?
arjun: hey all 44b i'm available to start remotely earlier if that helps. also curious about whether relocation stipend gets paid if my on-site start is delayed for visa reasons.
emily: quick summary: we need valid US work auth to run payroll (I-9). if waiver/alt pathway delays in-person start, we can either: 1) have you remain off-payroll and onboard remotely for non-billable tasks, or 2) consider contractor arrangement if you're outside US. relocation stipend is typically paid on first payroll check or a relocation milestone tied to physical start; we'll check policy exceptions.
natalie: from legal: waiver processing + any required consular processing could take 2-6+ months depending on government cadence. alternates: if Arjun qualifies for change-of-status to H-1 without waiver that'd be different, but with a 212(e) home-residency requirement waiver likely needed.
tom: team is flexible on remote ramp. production access and ssh creds only after payroll + background check clear. can we make an exception for code reviews / pairing?
emily: pairing + meetings are fine; no production deployments, no repo write access. we will create a "remote-limited" onboarding checklist.
arjun: re: equity cliff start & PTO accrual, will those be based on offer date or payroll start?
emily: equity vesting and PTO accrual anchor to payroll hire date. we can document the delay and sign an acknowledgement if you want to preserve offer terms, but the legal payroll date is authoritative for default grants. we can ask comp to consider backdating in exceptional cases, but it's not guaranteed.
benefits-bot: Note: benefit eligibility requires an active employee record. If hire_date >= 2026-09-01, health coverage effective = 1st of following month per vendor.
emily: relocation: policy normally pays on first payroll or reimbursement after receipt of move. if start shifts, we can do an advance in select cases; will need approval from finance. arjun, do you need advance?
arjun: might need partial advance to secure housing abroad pre-move. prefer to avoid complicated tax/contractor issues though.
natalie: two action items from counsel:
- Arjun: upload DS-2019 + passport copy to secure portal (redact non-needed PII)
- Counsel: confirm whether waiver intake submitted and estimate processing window within 5 business days
- People-ops: draft remote-limited onboarding checklist + relocation advance request flow
- Comp/Finance: advise on relocation advance tax treatment
tom: also confirm background check vendor can run pre-payroll if needed for remote hiring steps.
emily: will open HRIS ticket and route to finance/comp for relocation question. i'll DM the checklist link to Arjun. expected follow-ups by EOD tomorrow.
arjun: thanks. one more Q: if waiver is approved but requires consular stamping outside US, will Redwood cover travel costs for stamping?
emily: policy: travel for visa stamping is generally personal expense unless the company requests travel; relocation package may cover reasonable stamping travel when tied to onboarding. we'll review case-by-case.
natalie: will flag consular implications once intake is confirmed. also note: if travel is needed, consular appointment wait times vary by country. plan accordingly.
emily: summary of immediate next steps:
- Arjun: upload docs + confirm remote onboarding preferences
- Counsel (Natalie): confirm waiver intake status in 5bd
- People-ops: open HRIS ticket, draft onboarding checklist, route relocation query to finance
- Tom: OK with remote-limited ramp; no prod access until payroll done

tom: thanks all. keep me looped.
arjun: uploading docs now 4e4
